recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中一顆體積遠大於周邊細胞的巨大細胞，核呈多葉狀、胞質充滿紫紅色異染顆粒（metachromatic granules），免疫染色 CD117、CD25 與 tryptase 皆陽性，確認為巨大多葉肥大細胞（promastocyte）。
features: Giant cell many times the size of adjacent myeloid cells with multilobated/multiple overlapping nuclei
Abundant cytoplasm densely packed with purple-red metachromatic granules that spill into the surrounding background
Background marrow with dysplastic features including hypolobated/abnormally segmented neutrophils, blasts and immature myeloid cells
Immunostains: giant cell positive for CD117 and CD25 (red chromogen) and tryptase (brown)
Nuclear detail partly obscured by granules
describe_en: The bone marrow aspirate smear shows a giant cell with multilobated nuclei and abundant cytoplasm filled with coarse metachromatic granules, with granules scattered in the adjacent background. Surrounding hematopoietic cells include immature myeloid forms and granulocytes with abnormal nuclear segmentation. Immunocytochemistry shows the giant cell to be positive for CD117, CD25 and tryptase. Findings are consistent with giant multilobated atypical mast cells (promastocytes) in the setting of acute myeloid leukemia with myelodysplasia-related changes; evaluation for an associated systemic mastocytosis (KIT D816V) is warranted.

ddx.vs: Megakaryocytes have fine pink granules with platelet budding and are CD61/CD42b-positive but tryptase- and CD25-negative.
Basophils are smaller with water-soluble dark granules obscuring a lobated nucleus, and are tryptase-weak and CD117-negative.
Osteoclasts have many separate uniform nuclei and agranular or finely granular cytoplasm without tryptase positivity.
Mast cell leukemia requires ≥20% atypical mast cells on aspirate rather than isolated giant mast cells within an AML.
